findings.description: The prose is false. ADR 0141 and commit 2a5ae63 both say the inbox does not yet treat `retired` as it treats `landed`. That reader change is follow-up task t-mw6a2pfo, and until it lands the Needs-you line stays.
findings.body:
The `retireSession` JSDoc says the `retired` event "drops the session from the inbox". The code does not do that yet.

- `openPullRequest` in `src/core/dashboard.service.ts` (L741-L756) returns `undefined` only on a `landed` row. It skips every other row type (`if (event.type !== 'merge') continue;`), so a `retired` row is passed over and the newest `merge` is still returned.
- A retired session stays in state `merged`, and `dashboard.service.ts` L651 calls `openPullRequest` for every `merged` row. So after a retire, the session still shows `PR opened, not landed` in Needs you.
- Nothing under `src/` (tests aside) reads `retired` except the new writer and its own re-retire check.

ADR 0141 (L40-L44) defers this reader change to task t-mw6a2pfo: "until it lands the line stays". The PR description's acceptance says the opposite: "the session no longer appears in Needs you". A maintainer who trusts this JSDoc will close t-mw6a2pfo as already done, or file a bug when the line persists.

There are two ways to fix it:
- Fix the reader in this PR. That means `if (row.type === 'landed' || row.type === 'retired')` in both `openPullRequest` and `prFixRounds`, plus a test that asserts `needsYou` drops a retired session.
- Or reword the JSDoc (and the acceptance line) to say the event is recorded and t-mw6a2pfo clears the inbox line.

findings.description: `docs/conventions/naming.md` line 76 says: "`utils` | **Pure functions only.** Cannot import `service`, `manager`, `repository`, or `client`. If it needs one of those, it isn't a util." The new file imports `./git-diff.client.js` (`runGit`, `rethrowIfKilled`), `./merge-gate.service.js` (`deleteBranchAt`, `isAncestor`, `newestMerge`, `resolveCommit`) and `./session.repository.js` (`getSession`). Its functions also run git and read the database, so they are not pure. The next maintainer will either break the util contract or have to move the file.
findings.body:
`docs/conventions/naming.md` L76 says:

> `utils` | **Pure functions only.** Cannot import `service`, `manager`, `repository`, or `client`. If it needs one of those, it isn't a util.

This new file imports all three forbidden roles:

- `./git-diff.client.js`: `runGit`, `rethrowIfKilled`
- `./merge-gate.service.js`: `deleteBranchAt`, `isAncestor`, `newestMerge`, `resolveCommit`
- `./session.repository.js`: `getSession`

Its helpers also take a `Database` and run git (`worktree prune`, `worktree list`, `update-ref -d`), so they do I/O and are not pure. No ADR amends the rule. The file-naming hook only checks the suffix, so it won't catch this.

Pulling the teardown out of `land.service.ts` was the right call. But a module that does git and store I/O is a service. Rename it to `session-teardown.service.ts` and update the three importers: `land.service.ts`, `session-retire.service.ts` and `session-retire.test.ts`.

https://github.com/AlexisBalayre/pupitre/blob/9fff0286a0b38d1765c312bf7b2dbe0d703c1a8d/src/core/session-teardown.utils.ts#L1-L12

findings.description: `RetireOutcome` is an exported interface declared in a `*.service.ts` and imported by `src/cli/index.ts`, against `docs/conventions/general.md` §Type separation (exported types live in `src/core/types/*.types.ts`).
findings.body:
`docs/conventions/general.md` L75-L77 says:

> Exported types live in `*.types.ts` under the area's `types/` folder — `src/core/types/`, `src/adapters/types/`. **Never inline an exported or reused `type`/`interface` in a `*.service.ts` or `*.routes.ts` file**

L35-L36 says the same under "No inline types".

`export interface RetireOutcome` is declared at L43-L49 of this service, and `src/cli/index.ts:136` imports it: `import { type RetireOutcome, retireSession } from '../core/session-retire.service.js';`. The sibling `land.service.ts` follows the rule: it imports `LandOutcome` from `./types/land.types.js`.

Move `RetireOutcome` to `src/core/types/session-retire.types.ts` and import it from there in the service and in `index.ts`.

findings.description: Only the private `newestStanding` treats `retired` as ending a session's PR. The shared `newestMerge` reader (`merge-gate.service.ts`) still stops only at `landed`, so `pup land`, `pup fix` and `pup ci wait` on a retired session still see its merge as standing, and the follow-up inbox task has to chase every `newestMerge` caller instead of making one change.

`GIT_ENV`, `sh`, `commitIn`, `SESSION_ID`, `BRANCH`, `ORIGIN_URL` and `PR_URL` are copied from `src/test/helpers/land.mock.ts` and `git.mock.ts` instead of imported. A later fix to the git env isolation would then reach the land suites but miss this one.

The `retired` payload doc says the worktree and branch were removed, but the branch is kept when it holds commits past the pinned sha. Suggested wording: "removed the session's worktree and, unless it held commits past the pinned sha, its branch".

The only unit tests for `session-teardown.utils.ts` sit inside the retire suite, even though `pup land` now depends on those helpers too. Someone changing them for land will look for `session-teardown.test.ts` and not find these tests. Move the `describe('session teardown helpers')` block into its own file.

`pinnedPullRequest` takes a bare `untouched` string, while `assertStillMerged` and `assertUnlockedWorktree` in the same module take the whole `OriginUse`. Both callers already hold an `OriginUse`, and retire keeps a separate `UNTOUCHED` constant in sync with `RETIRE_USE`. Fix: take `use: OriginUse` in `pinnedPullRequest` as well.
